Hard freeze warning for South Texas

A hard freeze warning covers much of South and Central Texas through Thursday morning, with overnight lows expected to reach the low twenties in San Antonio and the surrounding Hill Country, the National Weather Service said Tuesday.

Forecasters warned that the freeze will last roughly twelve hours in some counties, long enough to burst exposed pipes and damage irrigation systems that were not drained after the last cold snap. Residents were urged to cover outdoor faucets and bring pets inside.

City officials opened four warming centers across Bexar County and said they would stay open through Friday if temperatures remain below freezing. Transit routes to each center will run on an extended schedule, and no fare will be collected for riders heading there.

The electric grid operator said it expects adequate supply but asked households to lower thermostats during the early morning peak. Officials stopped short of calling for conservation, saying reserves were well above the level that would trigger an alert.

Ranchers in the region reported moving livestock to sheltered pasture, and several school districts announced a two-hour delay. Road crews pretreated overpasses on the interstate corridor, where black ice has caused pileups in previous freezes.

Utility crews were staged overnight in anticipation of scattered outages. A spokesperson said restoration times could stretch if wind gusts bring down limbs already weakened by the drought that persisted through the autumn months across the region.
